name: Executive Order of March 23, 1874 establishing the Pyramid Lake Reservation
aka: Pyramid Lake Indian Reservation executive order
citation: Executive Order of March 23, 1874 (1 Kappler 869; Royce cessions 561 and 562)
promises: Not a treaty: a presidential order. President Grant set apart the Pyramid Lake Reservation in Nevada for the Paiute and other Indians, as surveyed in January 1865 (Royce 561).
The Indian Claims Commission held that the reservation was in fact established on November 29, 1859 by Interior Department action, and that the 1874 order formalised it.

The Commission held that the reservation carried with it sufficient Truckee River water to maintain Pyramid Lake, its fishery and the spawning reaches of the river, and that the United States had an obligation to preserve those waters and fisheries.
Royce records the rest of the Paiute country (Royce 562) under this entry as taken by the United States without formal relinquishment by the Indians.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that the Nevada portion of the Paviotso (western Nevada Paiute) lands outside the Pyramid Lake and Walker River reservations was taken by the United States without payment of compensation on December 31, 1862, the date those reservations had come into operation.

breaches.what: After the Commission ruled in 1973 that the reservation carried reserved Truckee River water and that the United States had a duty to preserve the lake and fishery, the tribe's claim for damages from not receiving all its water was settled by compromise for $8,000,000. The settlement stipulation says no water rights were lost by it.

landTaken: The Paviotso tract outside the reservations, taken without compensation on December 31, 1862 for the Nevada portion and March 3, 1853 for the California portion (Docket 87). The acreage was not read from an opened source.
compensation: Docket 87: net $15,790,000.00 for the Paviotso tract (final judgment, November 4, 1965). Docket 87-B: $8,000,000 compromise for water not received (July 23, 1975). The Commission also held the United States liable in 1972 for minerals and timber removed from the Nevada Paviotso tract between 1848 and December 31, 1862 (Docket 87-A); the amount was not found.
today: In its 1972 complaint in United States v. Nevada, quoted by the Commission in 1973, the United States said diversions from the Truckee River had dropped Pyramid Lake more than 70 feet since 1906, destroying fisheries. Docket 87-A was transferred to the Court of Claims in 1978; its outcome was not found.

openQuestions: Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe of Indians v. Morton, 354 F. Supp. 252 (D.D.C. 1972), which held the Secretary of the Interior's Truckee River regulation violated his trust duty to the tribe, could not be opened (Justia and CourtListener blocked the request); it would be a court-ruling breach once read.
The tribe's own history of the reservation was not located online; nationVoice is empty for that reason.
Nevada v. United States, 463 U.S. 110 (1983), which went against the tribe on its water claim, belongs in today once opened.
